note: How index.html builds each i18n/ui.en.json string that has {placeholders}, so its existing French and Portuguese can be found in i18n/translations.json and converted. Translations are filed under key(English as the page writes it), and the page writes ${...} holes or joins words with +, never {name}. One entry per placeholder key. "page" is a string from the memory, exactly as the page writes it; "holes" maps each ${...} in it to what replaces it (a {placeholder}, or "" for a hole whose value is always empty on this page). "parts" is for text the page joins with +: a plain string is copied as it is into every language (placeholders, spaces, punctuation); an object { t, holes?, drop? } is a memory string, translated, with its holes replaced and a leading "drop" removed. scripts/build-rbm-messages.js checks that the parts rebuild the English in ui.en.json exactly, and that every hole is found in each translation. See docs/rbm-messages-notes.md.
